_about: Prebuilt, verified sub-circuits. In a spec: "blocks": [{"use": "usb_c_power", "connect": {"VBUS": "VBUS"}}]. Nets starting with @ are ports: they join the spec net named in `connect` (default: `defaults`, else the port's own name). Optional ports left unconnected become no-connects. Other nets stay inside the block (named <block>_<net>). Refs are renumbered to fit the spec.

usb_c_power.title: USB-C 5 V power input (no data)
usb_c_power.description: Power-only USB-C receptacle with the two 5.1k CC pull-downs a host needs before it supplies 5 V, plus 10 uF bulk.

usb_c_data.title: USB-C with USB 2.0 data and ESD protection
usb_c_data.description: 16-pin USB-C (HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12) with 5.1k CC pull-downs, both D+/D- rows joined, a USBLC6-2SC6 ESD array right at the connector, and 10 uF bulk on VBUS.

nets.@GND: J1.GND J1.SHIELD R1.2 R2.2 U1.2 C1.2

ldo_ams1117_3v3.title: 3.3 V linear regulator, 1 A (AMS1117-3.3)
ldo_ams1117_3v3.description: AMS1117-3.3 in SOT-223 with 10 uF input and 22 uF output capacitors. Needs at least ~4.5 V in (not for 1S LiPo); dissipates (Vin - 3.3 V) x current.

ldo_ap2112_3v3.title: 3.3 V low-dropout regulator, 600 mA (AP2112K-3.3)
ldo_ap2112_3v3.description: AP2112K-3.3 (SOT-23-5) with 1 uF in and out, enable tied on. Low dropout, so it also works from a 1S LiPo down to ~3.5 V.

lipo_charger_mcp73831.title: Single-cell LiPo charger (MCP73831), with charge LED
lipo_charger_mcp73831.description: MCP73831-2 (4.2 V) with 4.7 uF in/out, PROG resistor setting the charge current (2k = 500 mA; current = 1000 V / R), and a red LED that lights while charging.

esp32_c3_wroom02.title: ESP32-C3 module (WROOM-02) with reset, boot and native USB
esp32_c3_wroom02.description: ESP32-C3-WROOM-02 with 10 uF + 100 nF at 3V3, EN pull-up and 1 uF delay with a RESET button, IO9 pull-up with a BOOT button, and native USB on IO18/IO19. IO2 and IO8 are strapping pins: don't pull them low at boot. Keep the antenna end at a board edge.

esp32_s3_wroom1.title: ESP32-S3 module (WROOM-1) with reset, boot and native USB
esp32_s3_wroom1.description: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 with 10 uF + 100 nF at 3V3, EN pull-up and 1 uF delay with a RESET button, IO0 pull-up with a BOOT button, and native USB on IO19/IO20 (USB_D-/USB_D+). IO3, IO45 and IO46 are strapping pins. Keep the antenna end at a board edge.

atmega328p_16mhz.title: ATmega328P (TQFP-32) at 16 MHz, Arduino-compatible core
atmega328p_16mhz.description: ATmega328P-AU with a 16 MHz crystal and 22 pF load caps, 100 nF on VCC, AVCC and AREF, and a 10k RESET pull-up. Program it over ISP (RESET, SCK=PB5, MISO=PB4, MOSI=PB3) or a UART bootloader (PD0/PD1).

ws2812b_led.title: Addressable RGB LED (WS2812B-2020) with decoupling
ws2812b_led.description: WS2812B-2020 with 100 nF at VDD. Chain several by connecting DOUT to the next block's DIN. At 5 V, a 3.3 V MCU may need a level shifter on DIN.

led_indicator.title: Indicator LED with series resistor
led_indicator.description: LED and resistor from a signal or supply (IN) to ground. 1k at 3.3 V gives ~1.3 mA for a red/green LED; use R = (V - Vf) / I.

button.title: Push button to ground
button.description: Tactile button pulling SIG to ground; use the MCU's internal pull-up, or add one.

i2c_pullups.title: I2C bus pull-ups
i2c_pullups.description: One pair of pull-ups per bus: 4.7k for 100 kHz (2.2k for 400 kHz or long buses).

qwiic_connector.title: Qwiic / STEMMA QT I2C connector (JST SH 4-pin)
qwiic_connector.description: JST SH 1 mm connector in the Qwiic pinout: 1 GND, 2 3V3, 3 SDA, 4 SCL.

lowside_switch.title: Low-side MOSFET switch for a load (AO3400A) with flyback diode
lowside_switch.description: Logic-level N-MOSFET (30 V, 5.7 A) switching the load's low side: 100R gate resistor, 100k gate pull-down, Schottky flyback diode across the load for motors, relays and solenoids.

voltage_divider.title: Voltage divider with filter cap (e.g. battery sense)
voltage_divider.description: OUT = IN x bottom / (top + bottom), with 100 nF on OUT for a quiet ADC reading. Defaults halve the input (100k/100k).

rp2040_minimal.title: RP2040 with 16 MB QSPI flash, 12 MHz crystal, USB, BOOTSEL and RESET
rp2040_minimal.description: Raspberry Pi RP2040 minimal system, from the hardware design guide and 14 open-source RP2040 boards: W25Q128JVS flash (JLCPCB basic), 12 MHz crystal (20 pF load) with 30 pF caps and a 1k XOUT resistor, 100 nF on every IOVDD/DVDD pin, 1 uF on VREG_VIN and VREG_VOUT (the internal 1.1 V core regulator feeds DVDD), 27R USB series resistors, BOOTSEL button (1k from QSPI_SS) and a RUN pull-up with RESET button. Keep the flash and crystal right next to the chip; USB_DP/USB_DN are a 90-ohm pair.
rp2040_minimal.support_note: 0.4 mm-pitch QFN-56: autorouting may leave a few connections near the chip on 2 layers; use 4 layers or finish them by hand in KiCad. Easier alternative: an ESP32-S3/C3 module.

nets.@+3V3: U1.IOVDD U1.ADC_AVDD U1.VREG_VIN U1.USB_VDD U2.VCC C3.1 C4.1 C5.1 C6.1 C7.1 C8.1 C11.1 C13.1 C14.1 C15.1 C16.1 R5.1 R6.1

stm32f103c8_core.title: STM32F103C8T6 ("Blue Pill" core) with 8 MHz crystal, USB, SWD and reset
stm32f103c8_core.description: STM32F103C8T6 LQFP-48: 100 nF on each VDD pin and VBAT plus 10 uF bulk, VDDA filtered with 100 nF + 1 uF, BOOT0 and BOOT1 (PB2) pulled low by 10k, NRST with 100 nF and a RESET button, 8 MHz crystal (20 pF load) on PD0/PD1 with 30 pF caps, and the 1.5k D+ pull-up USB full speed needs on PA12. SWD on PA13 (SWDIO) / PA14 (SWCLK).
stm32f103c8_core.support_note: LQFP-48 at 0.5 mm: usually routes on 2 layers with room around the chip; dense boards may need 4 layers.

nets.@+3V3: U1.VDD U1.VBAT U1.VDDA C3.1 C4.1 C5.1 C6.1 C7.1 C8.1 C9.1 R3.1

esp32_wroom32e.title: ESP32 module (WROOM-32E) with reset and boot buttons
esp32_wroom32e.description: ESP32-WROOM-32E with 10 uF + 100 nF at 3V3, EN 10k pull-up + 1 uF delay + RESET button, IO0 10k pull-up + BOOT button. Program over UART0 (TXD0/RXD0) with a USB-UART (ch340c_usb_uart + esp_autoprogram, or press BOOT while resetting). Strapping pins: IO12 must be low at boot (3.3 V flash), keep IO0, IO2, IO5, IO15 free at reset. IO34-39 are inputs only. Antenna end at a board edge with no copper under it.

ch340c_usb_uart.title: USB to UART (CH340C, no crystal) at 3.3 V
ch340c_usb_uart.description: WCH CH340C powered from 3.3 V (V3 tied to VCC, as the datasheet requires for 3.3 V operation) with 100 nF. UD+/UD- go straight to the USB connector's D+/D-. TXD is the CH340's output: wire it to the MCU's RX. DTR/RTS drive esp_autoprogram or an Arduino-style reset (100 nF in series to RESET).

esp_autoprogram.title: ESP32/ESP8266 auto-program circuit (DTR/RTS to EN/IO0)
esp_autoprogram.description: The two-transistor circuit from the NodeMCU/DevKit boards: esptool toggles DTR and RTS to reset the ESP into its bootloader, while both lines high or both low leave it running. Two MMBT3904 (JLCPCB basic) with 10k base resistors.

buck_ap63203_3v3.title: 3.3 V buck converter, 2 A (AP63203, 3.8-32 V in)
buck_ap63203_3v3.description: Diodes AP63203 synchronous buck at 1.1 MHz, values from its datasheet: 3.9 uH inductor (4x4 mm, 2.1 A), 10 uF + 100 nF input, 2x 22 uF output, 100 nF bootstrap; EN tied to VIN, FB to the output. Keep the input caps, chip and inductor in a tight loop with a solid ground under them; route SW short and wide, away from sensitive signals.

drv8833_motor.title: Dual DC motor / stepper driver (DRV8833, 2.7-10.8 V, 1.5 A per bridge)
drv8833_motor.description: TI DRV8833 in HTSSOP-16 with 10 uF + 100 nF on VM, 2.2 uF on VINT, 10 nF VCP to VM, nSLEEP pulled up to 3V3 (drive it low to sleep), nFAULT open-drain with a 10k pull-up, xISEN to GND (no current limiting). Inputs take 3.3 V logic (PWM xIN1/xIN2). Motor outputs carry amps: wide traces, and the thermal pad needs its ground vias.

nets.@GND: U1.GND U1.AISEN U1.BISEN C1.2 C2.2 C3.2

bme280_i2c.title: BME280 temperature / humidity / pressure sensor (I2C, address 0x76)
bme280_i2c.description: Bosch BME280 in I2C mode: CSB tied to VDDIO, SDO to GND (address 0x76; tie SDO to VDDIO for 0x77), 100 nF on VDD and VDDIO. Needs I2C pull-ups once per bus (i2c_pullups). Keep it away from regulators and the MCU, which warm it up; a slot in the board around it helps.

sht31_i2c.title: SHT31 temperature / humidity sensor (I2C, address 0x44)
sht31_i2c.description: Sensirion SHT31-DIS: ADDR to GND (0x44; to VDD for 0x45), R pin and thermal pad to VSS as the datasheet says, nRESET pulled up by 10k, 100 nF on VDD. ALERT is an optional output. Needs I2C pull-ups once per bus (i2c_pullups). Keep it away from heat sources.

mpu6050_i2c.title: MPU-6050 6-axis accelerometer + gyroscope (I2C, address 0x68)
mpu6050_i2c.description: InvenSense MPU-6050 per its datasheet: 100 nF REGOUT, 2.2 nF CPOUT, 10 nF on VLOGIC, 100 nF on VDD; CLKIN, FSYNC and AD0 to GND (address 0x68). INT is an optional interrupt output. Needs I2C pull-ups once per bus (i2c_pullups). Mount it near the board's centre, away from mounting holes and flex.

nets.@GND: U1.GND U1.CLKIN U1.FSYNC U1.AD0 C1.2 C2.2 C3.2 C4.2

ina219_current.title: INA219 current / power monitor with 0.1 ohm shunt (I2C, address 0x40)
ina219_current.description: TI INA219 with a 0.1 ohm 1206 shunt (JLCPCB basic) between IN+ (supply side) and IN- (load side): +-3.2 A range at 0.8 mA resolution, bus up to 26 V. A0/A1 to GND (0x40). Route IN+/IN- as a Kelvin pair straight from the shunt pads. Needs I2C pull-ups once per bus.

ads1115_adc.title: ADS1115 16-bit 4-channel ADC (I2C, address 0x48)
ads1115_adc.description: TI ADS1115 with ADDR to GND (0x48), 100 nF on VDD. Inputs AIN0-AIN3 must stay between GND and VDD; add an RC filter (1k + 100 nF) on noisy inputs. ALERT/RDY is optional (open drain, needs a pull-up). Needs I2C pull-ups once per bus.

ds3231_rtc.title: DS3231MZ real-time clock, +-5 ppm (I2C, address 0x68)
ds3231_rtc.description: Maxim DS3231MZ (SOIC-8) with 100 nF on VCC. VBAT goes to GND by default; connect it to a coin cell net (e.g. a CR2032 holder) to keep time without power. INT/SQW, RST and 32KHZ are optional open-drain pins. Note: same I2C address as the MPU-6050 (0x68) unless that one's AD0 is high.

micro_sd_spi.title: microSD card slot in SPI mode with card detect
micro_sd_spi.description: Molex 104031-0811 push-push microSD socket with 10 uF + 100 nF on VDD and 10k pull-ups on CMD, DAT0-DAT3 (the SD spec needs them; unused DAT1/DAT2 must not float). SPI mapping: CS = DAT3, MOSI = CMD, MISO = DAT0, SCK = CLK. CARD_DETECT closes to GND when a card is inserted (enable the MCU's pull-up). Place it at a board edge, socket opening outward.

rs485_transceiver.title: RS-485 half-duplex transceiver, 3.3 V (SP3485, JLCPCB basic)
rs485_transceiver.description: SP3485EN (pin-compatible with MAX3485) with 100 nF, ~RE and DE tied together as one direction pin (high = transmit), and a 120 ohm termination across A/B for the two ends of the bus ("omit": ["R1"] on middle nodes). RXD is the receiver output (to the MCU's RX), TXD the driver input. Add a TVS (SM712) on A/B for long cables.

can_sn65hvd230.title: CAN bus transceiver, 3.3 V (SN65HVD230)
can_sn65hvd230.description: TI SN65HVD230 with 100 nF, Rs to GND (high-speed mode, up to 1 Mbit/s), Vref unused, and a 120 ohm terminator across CANH/CANL for the two ends of the bus ("omit": ["R1"] on middle nodes). TXD/RXD go to the MCU's CAN controller (ESP32 TWAI, STM32 bxCAN). Route CANH/CANL as a pair.

level_shifter_bss138.title: Bidirectional logic level shifter, one channel (BSS138)
level_shifter_bss138.description: The classic open-drain level shifter: BSS138 with gate on the low-voltage rail and 10k pull-ups on both sides. Works for I2C and slow GPIO (up to ~400 kHz); use one block per signal (give each a "name"). Not for push-pull high-speed signals such as SPI above a few MHz.

reverse_polarity_pfet.title: Reverse-polarity protection with a P-MOSFET (AO3401A, up to 12 V)
reverse_polarity_pfet.description: Low-loss reverse-battery protection: AO3401A (JLCPCB basic, 30 V 4 A, ~50 mohm) with drain to the raw input and source to the protected rail; the gate goes to GND through 10k, so a reversed supply leaves it off. Gate-source rating limits this to inputs up to 12 V (add a 10 V zener gate-source above that).

input_protection_5v.title: 5 V input protection: resettable fuse + TVS
input_protection_5v.description: 500 mA polyfuse (1206, 6 V) in series with the 5 V input, then an SMAJ5.0A TVS from the protected rail to GND that clamps ESD and hot-plug spikes. For USB or 5 V DC inputs only (the fuse is rated 6 V). Put it right after the connector, before any regulator.

dc_jack_input.title: DC barrel jack input (5.5/2.1 mm, centre positive) with reverse protection
dc_jack_input.description: Through-hole barrel jack, an SS34 Schottky (3 A, JLCPCB basic) in series against reversed adapters, and 10 uF (50 V) + 100 nF bulk. Costs ~0.4 V; use reverse_polarity_pfet instead for lower loss. Feed it into a regulator (buck_ap63203_3v3, ldo_ams1117_5v0...). Jack footprint is generic: check it against the part you buy.

relay_5v.title: 5 V relay with transistor driver and flyback diode (SRD-05VDC, 10 A)
relay_5v.description: Songle-type SRD-05VDC-SL-C relay (72 mA coil) switched by an MMBT3904 from a 3.3 V GPIO through 1k, with a 10k base pull-down so it stays off at boot and a 1N4148W flyback diode across the coil. COM/NO/NC are the contacts. For mains voltages keep 6+ mm clearance and cut a slot between the contact side and the low-voltage side, and have it reviewed.

buzzer_driver.title: Magnetic buzzer with transistor driver
buzzer_driver.description: 12 mm magnetic buzzer driven by an MMBT3904 from a GPIO (1k base, 10k pull-down), with a 1N4148W across the coil. Drive CTRL with a ~2-4 kHz PWM (passive buzzer) or high (active buzzer).

ldo_ams1117_5v0.title: 5 V linear regulator, 1 A (AMS1117-5.0)
ldo_ams1117_5v0.description: AMS1117-5.0 (JLCPCB basic) with 10 uF (50 V) input and 22 uF output. Needs at least ~6.5 V in; dissipates (Vin - 5 V) x current, so above ~12 V in or a few hundred mA use a buck converter.

ldo_xc6206_3v3.title: 3.3 V low-power LDO, 200 mA (XC6206, JLCPCB basic)
ldo_xc6206_3v3.description: Torex XC6206P332MR in SOT-23 with 1 uF in and out: 1 uA quiescent current, good for battery sensors. Input 6 V max (USB or 1S LiPo, not 9-12 V); 200 mA max, so not for Wi-Fi modules (use ldo_ams1117_3v3, ldo_ap2112_3v3 or buck_ap63203_3v3).

lipo_charger_tp4056.title: 1S LiPo charger, up to 1 A (TP4056)
lipo_charger_tp4056.description: TP4056 linear charger (4.2 V) with 10 uF on input and battery, NTC input disabled (TEMP to GND), CE tied to VCC. Charge current = 1200 / R_PROG: "prog": "2k" gives 600 mA (default), "1.2k" 1 A. CHRG and STDBY are open-drain status outputs (for LEDs to VBUS through 1k, or MCU pins with pull-ups). The exposed pad is GND and spreads heat: at 1 A it dissipates up to ~1 W.

nets.@GND: U1.GND U1.TEMP U1.EPAD C1.2 C2.2 R1.2

swd_header.title: SWD programming header (1x5, 2.54 mm)
swd_header.description: 3V3, SWDIO, SWCLK, NRST, GND on a 2.54 mm header for an ST-Link, J-Link or Raspberry Pi Debug Probe. For STM32 and RP2040 (RP2040 has RUN in place of NRST).

uart_header.title: UART header (1x4, 2.54 mm: GND, RX, TX, 3V3)
uart_header.description: Serial console header. Pins are labelled from the board's side: wire the adapter's TX to RX here and RX to TX. Pin 4 supplies or takes 3V3; leave it unconnected on the adapter if the board has its own power.

oled_i2c_header.title: I2C OLED display header (SSD1306/SH1106 0.96" module: GND, VCC, SCL, SDA)
oled_i2c_header.description: 4-pin socket in the pin order of the common 0.96" and 1.3" I2C OLED modules (GND, VCC, SCL, SDA; some modules swap GND and VCC, so check yours). The modules have their own pull-ups on most versions.
